# Drywall patching

Americans say drywall, the bloke at Travis Perkins says plasterboard, I say "the hole the door handle made".

## The damage

- Back bedroom, behind the door. No door stop, so the lever handle went through the stud wall the day the wind slammed it (Sept 2024). Hole roughly 70mm x 90mm
- Landing: two old screw holes and a rawlplug crater where the previous owners had a big mirror
- Hallway: the cable chase I cut in 2023 for the new hallway light switch, already filled once and cracked along one edge

## Small holes and the cable chase

- Raked out loose bits, brushed, damp sponge
- Toupret Fill & Fix (the pink-goes-white one), overfilled slightly, sanded flush with 120 then 180 grit
- Cable chase crack came back because I filled it too deep in one go last time. This time two layers, a day apart, with scrim tape over the joint first

## The big hole

Too big for filler alone. Options I looked at:
1. Self-adhesive aluminium mesh patch, 150mm x 150mm, £3.80. Quick, a bit lumpy under paint
2. California patch: cut a piece of board bigger than the hole, score the back, peel away the gypsum leaving the paper flange
3. Proper job: cut back to the studs and screw in a new piece

Went with option 2. Offcut of 12.5mm Gyproc from the loft, cut it 30mm bigger than the hole all round, traced the core on the wall, opened the hole up square with a padsaw, buttered the edges with Easi-Fill 20, pressed in, feathered the paper flange out with a 150mm taping knife. Three coats in total, sanded between. About 2.5 hours over two evenings.

## Finishing

Mist coat of watered down emulsion first because fresh filler sucks paint in and flashes. Then two coats of the same white as the rest of the room (Dulux Trade Vinyl Matt, Pure Brilliant White). You can just about see it at a low angle with a torch. Nobody's going to do that.

Bought a door stop. £2.20. Should've done that first.

See [[Painting the hallway]] for the hallway walls and [[Fuse box labels]] for which circuit the hallway switch is on.
